title: add-runtime-nvtx-counters-and-microbench-perf-dashboard
author: Maya Chen
description: Add NVTX ranges, lightweight runtime counters, and a microbenchmark harness + perf dashboard to help diagnose kernel/scheduling/KV-cache/continuous-batching regressions. Motivation: we recently observed variability in tail latency across model variants and hardware; this PR adds deterministic NVTX ranges around key runtime stages (kernel dispatch, KV cache hit/miss, batching enqueue/dequeue, scheduler queue time), exposes per-worker counters for token counts and queue wait time, and adds a microbench runner and Grafana dashboard config to visualize those metrics. Key items: 1) NVTX: minimal overhead scoped ranges around init, forward, pack_kv, apply_kv, schedule_loop, batch_assemble, batch_dispatch. 2) Counters: atomic counters exposed via /metrics and internal registry: kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, batch_size_histogram, schedule_queue_time_ms, worker_idle_ms. 3) Microbench: bench_runner can replay synthetic workloads (prefix-heavy, streaming, short-turn, long-turn) against a single worker or cluster; includes deterministic seed and configurable sampling. 4) Perf dashboard: Grafana json + Prometheus scrape job example and README with runbook for interpreting charts. Checklist: [x] NVTX ranges added and gated behind REDWOOD_NVTX env var (off by default), [x] counters implemented and exported, [x] microbench harness + tests, [x] dashboard json and docs, [x] added unit tests for counter registration and a microbench integration test. This change is backwards-compatible and opt-in; NVTX and microbench are disabled in production builds by default. See commits for implementation details and CI for test runs.

feat(runtime): emit runtime counters and register with telemetry registry
feat(bench): add tools/microbench/bench_runner.py and workload configs
docs(perf): add perf dashboard json and README with runbook
test(perf): add unit/integration tests for counters and microbench harness
chore(ci): add microbench job to CI (sanity, not perf runs)
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall looks good. Please make NVTX opt-in via env var and ensure the overhead is negligible for high-throughput paths.
Maya Chen (author): NVTX is gated behind REDWOOD_NVTX and compiles out when NVTX_SUPPORT=0. We also sample only 1% of requests by default in high-throughput clusters; config documented in README.

Sofia Martinez: Can you add a unit test that verifies counters are registered and exposed to the telemetry registry before the worker starts? Also add a cleanup hook so tests don't leak registry state.
Maya Chen (author): Added tests/unit/test_counters_registration.cpp and a registry reset helper; CI updated to cover cleanup.
Ben Goldberg: Dashboard looks useful — please add the dashboard url and an example query for diagnosing KV cache miss storms in the runbook.
Maya Chen (author): Added example PromQL queries and a short runbook section explaining KV cache miss interpretation and mitigation (pin to LRU, warm prefixes).
Arjun Patel: One nit: scheduler queue time uses ms histogram; consider also publishing p99/p999 as gauges for alerting. Not blocking.
Maya Chen (author): Good suggestion — added p99/p999 exported as derived gauges in counters.cpp. Updated docs.
Ben Goldberg: Approving after CI green.
ci_checks: unit-tests: failed (initially failed on test_counters_registration due to registry leak) -> fix pushed -> passed
release_notes:
- Add opt-in NVTX instrumentation for runtime stages (REDWOOD_NVTX)
- Expose lightweight runtime counters: kv_cache_hits/misses, batch_size_histogram, schedule_queue_time_ms, worker_idle_ms
- Add microbench harness to reproduce kv-cache and batching scenarios
- Add Grafana dashboard + Prometheus scrape example to help diagnose regressions
notes_for_reviewers: Benchmarks included in tools/microbench are intended for dev/local perf investigations; CI does not run full perf suites. When enabling NVTX in staging, watch for increased overhead; NVTX is disabled by default in production builds.
